business_problem: Credit Saison wanted to understand how AI could improve everyday work and deliver tangible results across its workforce. Retail teams spent time documenting daily debriefs, corporate sales needed to research customer challenges and improve proposals, and inside sales needed more opportunities for newer employees to practice conversations without drawing experienced colleagues away from selling.
solution_summary: Credit Saison piloted ChatGPT Enterprise with 315 participants before rolling it out to all employees in September 2025. Teams use custom GPTs inside existing work: retail staff feed in audio from daily debriefs and receive summaries of results, meeting notes, handovers, and focus areas; corporate sales uses a company-research GPT to identify customer challenges and prepare proposals; inside sales employees practice prospect conversations by voice and receive feedback. A shareholder-meeting simulation also helped leaders explore voice interactions, while leaders used a custom GPT for company research. OpenAI provided executive training and beginner workshops; the CoE shared adoption lessons in a dedicated Slack channel. The story names no underlying data stores, model configuration, or technical system integrations. It separately reports engineering use of Codex.

data_flow: Retail teams use audio from daily debriefs as input to a custom GPT, which generates performance summaries, notes, handovers, and focus areas. Inside sales employees use voice to role-play with a GPT and receive feedback. The source does not describe storage or downstream system flows.
business_outcome: The pilot delivered a reported 954% ROI and saved 14 hours per employee each month, exceeding Credit Saison's initial targets. Survey respondents reported that ChatGPT Enterprise improved their work and job satisfaction. The pilot results led to a companywide rollout decision within one month of its completion.
